chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Driving back to Canada in snow with pianist Wilkins
summary: After leave in the States he rode with pianist Wilkins and a drink at a club, reluctant to return to the job, with the dash lights failing in falling snow on a narrow Vermont highway.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Who did you have in the trio?
Wilkins was his first name.
Was he the drummer, or --
The piano. He was -- it was his car that we was riding in when we left the highway, turned over and over and over, and when we finished I was wrapped around the steering wheel, and broke my hip.
I'm sure this is not something you
want to relive too much, Herman, but how did the whole thing happen? Why were you coming back to the States at this point?
No, we had left the States, and going back to the job.
Oh, oh. You had --
Yeah, we were going back. Yeah, I didn't want to go --
You had left the job, and you were going back to it.
Yeah.
I see.

I didn't want to go. We were on -- had been home on leave, and -- and (unintelligible) just to take the -- we'd been off of the job, and I told them I wasn't sure -- I didn't want to go back, and it's a matter of running out on the guys. He said well, come on back until we can get somebody, and so we can -- the drummer, and I, want to make it. I mean the drummer and the piano player say we'll make it, and you know, come on back until I grab -- get somebody.

I said well, okay. I don't want to leave them hanging, you know. You don't walk away and leave a guy when he needs you. So we'd been riding all day, and a big Lincoln car, and we got about 30 miles of our destination. That's when it happened. The lights went out on the car, and we

left the highway, and went over, and then back, and then missed a hole about 20 feet deep with water in it. Turned over and over and over. I don't know how many times, and [ ] came and said he was only doing 35 miles an hour, and I was in the hospital seven months with a broken hip, and I'm still suffering with it, and I've got to go back in the hospital maybe next week and let them take the pin out that they put in there, which has -- was broke about a year ago.
And I've got to go back in the hospital now and let them take it --
Do you know why he went off the road?
Uh -- because the lights went out on the dash.
Just the lights went out? I mean he just went right out, huh?
Yeah, when the lights -- it was about 6:00 o'clock in the evening, and snow had just started falling.
Oh, snow, too.
Yeah, and --
Oh, I see.
Yeah, and the lights went out on the dashboard, and you can't see where you're driving, and they had very thin -- not -- rather narrow highway with the saddleback, what you call the saddleback road?
Oh yeah, the hump, and --

Yeah, and one car go this way, and another one car comes out, and you know. And we knew, hadn't been traveling the highway, what I say, two or three years, that we knew it. But when it's dark, it's dark, and who knows? The man -- now, the man wasn't drinking -- we'll we'd stopped for about 15 minutes, maybe, and I knew the people who owned the club, and we had a drink. I had one drink -- that's -- and he had one. And we were rushing because we only had 30 miles to go, and it was about dinner time.

We wanted to get in and have a dinner before going to bed, so my friend in this club says stay here, Herman. I'll -- we'll have dinner here, and I'll drive you over there. I said Naah, I'm just going -- you know, riding all day, you know.
Oh boy. Yeah.

Been riding all day, I might as well go on in, so had I stayed there with him I'd have been better off, you know. And on the way out the lights went off again, because I was sitting there. Had my leg folded just like that, kind of crossed, and and then I'd doze off, maybe, you know. I had a couple of drinks, or one drink. I'd been riding all day.
